top_choice_rationale: Car and Parrinello's extended Lagrangian let electrons and nuclei evolve together, making first-principles dynamics of bond breaking, solvation and condensed-phase chemistry practical without a pre-built force field. It is new, forty years mature, reimplemented in many independent codes, and it underlies ab initio and QM/MM treatments and the reference data for machine-learned potentials. Attribution is two names with no priority dispute. The main weakness is that Born-Oppenheimer ab initio MD now does much of the same work, so the citation must rest on the conceptual unification. Perovskites (Miyasaka, Park, Snaith) follow as a clean trio but with unresolved stability, then ionizable lipid nanoparticles, where the three-name cut is contestable and Medicine 2023 sits adjacent.
recusal_note: Computational biochemist from the Warshel school; Car-Parrinello is adjacent to my own simulation field (QM/MM and EVB) and a possible field-closeness conflict, though no personal tie to Car or Parrinello is apparent from the profile.
